drift: White text on Header Orange (#FA8B39) is about 2.4:1, app-wide (Dashboard, Advisories, Billing, Alerts). Recorded as the world's material, not as a passing contrast; unresolved.
Colours are raw hex final fields per screen state, not Material ColorScheme roles; no ThemeData and no dark theme exist.
Neutrals vary: textDark #1E1E1E (Advisories, Settings, Billing) vs #111418 (Alerts); ground #FAFAFA vs Billing's creamBg #FFFDF9.
Billing names a different orange family: primaryOrange #FCB775, brandOrangeText #E25319, tier text #7A3712, active tab #EF7A22.
Dashboard content cards use a Colors.grey 35% border plus 2 to 5% black shadows; Advisories cards use the 1px #ECECEC hairline with no shadow. The hairline is recorded as canonical.
Dashboard header glass tiles carry a 12px backdrop blur over the flat field; Advisories drops it.
Alerts has no flat orange header: a 22% orange radial glow behind a dark 30px title.
Alerts passes Signal Orange (#F26E22) to BakitExpander, and the expander defaults to it: about 2.9:1 on white. Advisories passes Orange Ink.
Uppercase tracked labels exist in Billing calculator captions (BILL CALCULATOR, 11px/800, 0.8 tracking) and Alerts severity tags (1.2 tracking); not canonized.

narrative.overview:
GRID reads like the face of a household electric meter turned warm: a flat orange field across the top of the screen where the live numbers sit in translucent white tiles and roll digit by digit like meter wheels, and a quiet off-white desk below where cards explain what those numbers mean. The orange field is where the household looks; the desk is where it reads. Dashboard and Advisories are built this way; Billing, Alerts and Settings predate it and carry older variants (see drift notes in the sidecar).

Density is moderate and phone-first: one column, 16 to 20px gutters, a floating white pill nav that the content scrolls under. Depth is mostly flat. The system leans on Material 3 defaults (Roboto, stock TabBar, FilterChip, buttons and ripples) re-coloured per screen with raw hex fields; there is no custom ThemeData and no dark theme. Charts are custom-painted directly onto the orange field and respond to touch: hold or tap a point and the header tiles re-read for it, with a selection haptic per step; release returns to the live state.

Motion is functional and always optional: bars rise once, digits roll, labels swap, and every animation collapses to zero under the system's Remove animations setting.
keyCharacteristics: Flat orange header field with white type and translucent white glass tiles.
Off-white ground with white cards edged by a single hairline rule at 20px radius.
Numbers that change roll per digit with tabular figures.
Painted, touch-scrubbable charts living inside the header, not in cards.
Roboto at heavy Material weights (700 to 900) for every number and title.
A floating, blurred white pill as the only navigation chrome.

rules.name: The Ink Swap Rule
rules.body: Orange that is read as text on white is Orange Ink, never Signal Orange. Signal Orange is for fills, indicators and icons on white; Header Orange is for the field.

rules.name: The White On Field Rule
rules.body: Everything on the header field is white or translucent white (tiles at 30% to 8% white, borders at 40%, unselected chips at 18%, last-week bars at 38%). No second hue enters the field except data colour inside white pills.

rules.name: The Raw Hex Rule
rules.body: Colours are declared as `final Color` fields at the top of each screen state using the names above (primaryOrange, topCardColor, bgColor, textDark, orangeInk, hairline). New screens copy these fields verbatim rather than inventing neighbours.

rules.name: The Weight Not Face Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from Roboto's weights and size, never from a second family, uppercase tracking or decorative styling.

rules.name: The Scale With The System Rule
rules.body: Type follows the system font-size setting. Long labels shrink (FittedBox scale-down) or ellipsize; they do not clip.

rules.name: The Float Earns Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only floating overlays cast a shadow. Cards resting on the ground are edged by a hairline rule, not lifted.

rules.name: The Blur Must See Something Rule
rules.body: Backdrop blur is used where content actually moves behind the surface (the nav pill, blur 8). Over the flat orange field a blur shows nothing and costs a full pass on budget phones, so header tiles are translucent gradients without blur.

dos: **Do** start a screen from the header field: flat Header Orange (#FA8B39) to the status bar, white headline at 24px/800, glass tiles at 20px radius.
**Do** put orange text on white in Orange Ink (#C2501A) and keep Signal Orange (#F26E22) for fills, indicators and icons.
**Do** edge resting cards with a 1px Hairline (#ECECEC) at 20px radius on the Ground (#FAFAFA).
**Do** use RollingNumber for any value that updates live or on scrub, and SwapText for the label above it.
**Do** make header charts scrubbable with a selection haptic per step and a return on release.
**Do** read `MediaQuery.disableAnimationsOf` and collapse every duration to zero when it is set.
**Do** give every data source a loading, empty, offline and error state using the state card.
**Do** keep tap targets at 48dp and let text scale with the system setting.
donts: **Don't** set Signal Orange (#F26E22) as text on white; at about 2.9:1 it fails body contrast.
**Don't** lift resting cards with shadows; shadows belong to the nav pill and hint pills only.
**Don't** add backdrop blur over the flat orange field.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface, uppercase tracked eyebrows or caption kickers above sections.
**Don't** invent new neutrals; reuse Ink, Body Ink, Muted Ink and Ground rather than near-duplicates.
**Don't** colour data in red or green unless it is a direction (rise or fall).
